note: Card width == typical adult total length (tl, mm) in aquaria; snails: crawling length. aspect = card height / width (computed from the art when omitted). art = a drawing key in src/art (placeholder.ts hand-drawn, fishgen.ts generated, snails.ts). zone 'bottom' rests on the substrate; kind 'snail' clings to the floor or a glass pane. habitat 'land' rests on ground above the water, 'both' on land or in water deep enough (default 'water'). group 'school' swims in a tight, aligned school, 'shoal' in a loose group (when 3+ are kept); level 'top' / 'low' is the part of the water column a swimmer favours (default mid). Both only steer Shuffle. Lengths are total length, nose to tail tip (Nathan 2026-10-08). cat = the Animals menu it is listed under: 'fw-fish' (default), 'fw-invert', 'sw-fish', 'sw-invert', 'amphibian', 'reptile', 'land-invert'. female = the female's drawing and adult length for a sexually dimorphic species (the species itself is the male).

species.name: Dwarf pencilfish
species.note: Peaceful, keeps to the middle and upper water; a classic dither for Apistogramma and other dwarf cichlids (Seriously Fish).

species.name: Green neon tetra
species.note: Soft, acidic, stable water; 8-10 or more (Seriously Fish rates it moderate: needs an established tank).

species.name: Strawberry rasbora
species.note: Tiny and timid; a school of 8-10 or more in a planted tank, fed small live or frozen foods (Seriously Fish).

species.name: Exclamation point rasbora
species.note: The smallest of the nano rasboras; keeps to cover in a group of 8-10 or more (Seriously Fish).

species.name: Dwarf spotted rasbora
species.note: Timid nano schooler, 8-10 or more; not an ideal community fish at this size (Seriously Fish).

species.name: Black skirt tetra
species.note: Hardy, but may nip the long fins of bettas, angelfish and fancy guppies. Keep six or more.

species.name: White cloud mountain minnow
species.note: Cool water, about 18-22 °C; no heater needed in most rooms.

species.name: Boeseman's rainbowfish
species.note: Males reach about 10 cm, rarely 14 (FishBase).

species.name: Endler's livebearer
species.note: A small livebearer for hard, alkaline water; males are about 1 in, females a little larger. Keep several females per male (Seriously Fish).

species.name: Glass catfish
species.note: A transparent, timid schooler for dim, planted water: at least 6 (Seriously Fish).

species.name: Yoyo loach
species.note: Active and boisterous: groups of 5-6 or more, preferably 10; can nip long, slow fins and jumps, so it needs a tight lid (Seriously Fish).

species.name: Clown pleco
species.note: A small wood-eating pleco, 3.5-4 in; needs driftwood to graze; peaceful, though males may fight over territory (Aquarium Source).

species.name: Salt and pepper corydoras
species.note: One of the smallest corys; a group of at least 4-6, ideally 10 or more (Seriously Fish).

species.name: Firemouth cichlid
species.note: Not especially aggressive but territorial when breeding and may eat much smaller fish; best as a pair, gregarious outside spawning (Seriously Fish).

species.name: Neon dwarf rainbowfish
species.note: Keep a shoal of at least 6-8, preferably more; males deepen and colour up with age (Seriously Fish).

species.name: False julii corydoras
species.note: Most fish sold as julii cory are really this species (Seriously Fish); a group of at least 6.

species.name: Peacock gudgeon
species.note: Somewhat territorial with its own kind but peaceful with other small fish; start with 6-8 young fish and let them pair (Seriously Fish).

species.name: Clown killifish
species.note: Peaceful but tiny and specialised, with soft acidic water; buy 8-10 or more (Seriously Fish).

species.name: Electric blue acara
species.note: A captive blue colour form of the blue acara: peaceful for a cichlid, breeds readily; 6-7 in (Aquarium Source, Seriously Fish for the wild fish).

species.name: Convict cichlid
species.note: Violent when breeding, will attack fish several times its size; a species or pair tank (Seriously Fish).

species.name: Glowlight tetra
species.note: A peaceful schooler: at least 6, ideally 10 or more (Seriously Fish).

species.name: Common pleco
species.note: Sold at 3-4 in but a captive adult reaches about 15 in (24 in in the wild) and needs 75-80 gal or more; adults turn territorial and very messy (Aquarium Source).

species.name: Three-spot gourami
species.note: Sold as blue, gold and opaline forms; males are territorial and some turn spiteful as they mature (Seriously Fish).

species.name: Sparkling gourami
species.note: A tiny, slow labyrinth fish, 40 mm SL (Seriously Fish): hovers among plants, breathes air at the surface and makes soft croaking sounds. Peaceful; keep it with equally small, calm fish and avoid strong flow.

species.name: Croaking gourami
species.note: A slender, slow labyrinth fish to about 70 mm SL (Seriously Fish), peaceful unless breeding; both sexes croak. Needs a planted, shady tank with surface cover and a tight lid (an excellent jumper).

species.name: Cockatoo dwarf cichlid
species.note: Males up to 9 cm, females about 5 cm (FishBase).

species.name: Yellow lab cichlid
species.note: Lake Malawi mbuna: hard, alkaline water; up to about 10 cm.

species.name: Peacock cichlid
species.note: Lake Malawi haplochromine: hard, alkaline water; males to about 13 cm, females about 10 cm.

species.name: Demasoni cichlid
species.note: Small Lake Malawi mbuna, very aggressive for its size: keep a large group; about 7 cm.

species.name: Kadango (red-fin) cichlid
species.note: Lake Malawi open-water haplochromine: males to about 17 cm, females about 14 cm.

species.name: Blue-nosed mbuna
species.note: Lake Malawi mbuna with a fleshy, overhanging snout for scraping algae: hard, alkaline water; males to about 12 cm.

species.name: Golden mbuna
species.note: Lake Malawi mbuna: the male is dark with pale stripes, the female gold with black. Aggressive; to about 11 cm.

species.name: Livingstone's cichlid
species.note: Lake Malawi predator that lies on the sand playing dead to ambush small fish: big tanks only; to about 20 cm.

species.name: Dogtooth cichlid
species.note: Lake Malawi mbuna: blue and black barred with a yellow dorsal; to about 10 cm.

species.name: Malawi synodontis
species.note: Lake Malawi catfish: hard, alkaline water; to about 15 cm; shy by day, a good mbuna tank-mate.

species.name: Comet goldfish
species.note: Single-tailed goldfish; grows to 30 cm, best in a pond or a very large tank.

species.name: Peppered corydoras
species.note: Tolerates cooler water than most tropical fish, about 64-75 °F; females to about 3 in, males smaller.

species.name: Pygmy corydoras
species.note: Often hovers in mid-water shoals; females to about 3 cm.

species.name: Sterba's corydoras
species.note: A warm-water cory, about 24-28 °C (Seriously Fish): a usual bottom companion for rams.

species.name: Clown loach
species.note: Commonly 15-20 cm in aquaria; can reach 30 cm.

species.name: Bala shark
species.note: Not a true shark: a big, fast open-water minnow, 300-350 mm SL (Seriously Fish), that needs a school of 5+ and about a 240 x 60 cm tank; eats very small fish and jumps, so keep a tight lid.

species.name: Rainbow shark
species.note: Slate grey-blue minnow with red-orange fins, to about 150 mm SL (Seriously Fish). Keep one per tank: it grows territorial and attacks look-alikes, red-tail sharks above all. Needs caves and cover. The albino form is widely sold.

species.name: Red-tail shark
species.note: Velvet-black minnow with a red tail, to about 125 mm SL (Seriously Fish). Keep one per tank: it grows territorial and attacks look-alikes such as rainbow sharks. Needs caves and cover.

species.name: Reticulated hillstream loach
species.note: Needs cool, fast-flowing, oxygen-rich water; grazes on rock and glass.

species.name: Orange dwarf crayfish (CPO)
species.note: Eats small shrimp, shrimplets and may grab slow bottom fish; escapes an open top.

species.name: Cajun dwarf crayfish
species.note: The smallest crayfish; may grab slow bottom fish and snack on shrimp or fry; escapes an open top.

species.name: Red swamp crayfish
species.note: Aggressive and destructive: eats plants, snails, shrimp and small or slow fish; one per tank; an invasive species and restricted in some places; needs a tight lid.

species.name: Redclaw crayfish
species.note: Large Australian crayfish to about 25 cm with claws; eats most fish it can catch, plants and invertebrates; one per tank; needs a lid.

species.name: Thai micro crab
species.note: About 1 cm across; shy, lives among moss and roots, filter-feeds with its fan-like claws; may leave the water.

species.name: Aquatic isopod (water slater)
species.note: A detritus eater that clears leaf litter; breeds in a colony and is prey for most fish; sold by some aquarium shops and online dealers (Pond Informer).

species.name: Ocellaris clownfish
species.note: Up to 11 cm (FishBase).

species.name: Yellow tang
species.note: Up to 20 cm (FishBase).

species.name: Blue tang
species.note: Up to 31 cm (FishBase); needs a very large reef tank.

species.name: Kole tang
species.note: About 7 in (hobby pages; FishBase 15.4 cm SL). A reef-safe algae grazer; one per tank, since it fights other bristletooth tangs.

species.name: Foxface rabbitfish
species.note: 8-10 in (hobby pages; FishBase 25 cm SL). A peaceful herbivore with venomous fin spines that can sting painfully; one per tank, and underfed it nips corals.

species.name: Flame angelfish
species.note: 4-5.5 in in aquaria (retail pages; FishBase 15 cm). Reef safe with caution, since it may nip corals; a semi-aggressive dwarf angel, one per tank unless a large tank and a planned harem.

species.name: Lawnmower blenny
species.note: 4-6 in (hobby pages; FishBase 14 cm). A solitary algae scraper that needs a mature tank; keep one, since it fights other blennies.

species.name: Orchid dottyback
species.note: About 3 in (retail pages; FishBase 6.3 cm). Reef safe, but intolerant of other dottybacks and of fish of similar size, shape or colour; keep one.

species.name: Pajama cardinalfish
species.note: About 3.3 in (Wikipedia). Peaceful, nocturnal and best in a small school; the male mouthbroods.

species.name: Yellowtail blue damselfish
species.note: About 3 in (Wikipedia, LiveAquaria). The mildest of the damsels, but still semi-aggressive and territorial; males guard eggs.

species.name: Tailspot blenny
species.note: About 2.5 in (hobby pages; Wikipedia says 6 cm). A peaceful, reef-safe algae grazer that jumps; keep one, since it fights other blennies.

species.name: Mandarin dragonet
species.note: Picks copepods off the rock all day; needs a mature reef.

species.name: Skunk cleaner shrimp
species.note: Body length; the white antennae reach about as far again.

species.name: Blue-leg hermit crab
species.note: Length including its borrowed shell.

species.name: African dwarf frog
species.note: Fully aquatic; swims up for air. Not the African clawed frog, which grows to 12 cm.

species.name: Crested gecko (flame)
species.note: Arboreal; climbs glass and branches on its toe pads; prehensile tail.

species.name: Crested gecko (harlequin)
species.note: Arboreal; climbs glass and branches on its toe pads; prehensile tail.

species.name: Green anole
species.note: About 5 g and 15-20 cm with the tail (the male larger). Climbs branches, foliage and glass on its toe pads; turns from green to brown with temperature and mood; the male's pink dewlap shows when he displays. Needs UVB, a basking spot of 32-35 C and misted leaves to drink from.

species.name: Green anole (brown phase)
species.note: The same lizard in its brown colour phase (cool, stressed or on bark). About 5 g; climbs on its toe pads; needs UVB and a warm basking spot.

species.name: Brown anole
species.note: Males about 17-20 cm with the tail and females about 12-14 cm. The stockier anole: spends more time low on trunks and the ground than the green anole; the male's orange-red dewlap has a yellow edge. Needs UVB and a basking spot of 32-35 C. Keep one male per enclosure.

species.name: Leopard gecko
species.note: Ground dweller; no toe pads, so it does not climb glass.

species.name: Regal jumping spider
species.note: Body length: the male about 12 mm, black with white bands and white palps; the female about 15 mm, grey-brown. Climbs glass and branches; the legs span about twice that.

species.name: Ball python
species.note: Adult 1.0-1.5 m (a female larger); a hatchling is about 25 cm. Rests coiled, curls into a ball when alarmed, drapes over and wraps round branches; does not climb glass. The enclosure should be about as long as the snake: pick the size to fit the tank.

species.name: Chaco golden knee tarantula
species.note: Body length: the male about 45 mm, the female about 50 mm; leg span 12-15 cm. A docile terrestrial New World tarantula: dark with pale golden knees and rose-brown hair. Lives on the floor and in a hide; rears up with the front legs raised when threatened.

species.name: Mexican red knee tarantula
species.note: Body about 5 cm, leg span 13-14 cm. A docile terrestrial tarantula that burrows and lives in a hide: black with a rust-red knee band, orange-red hair on the abdomen. Slow, flicks urticating hairs when alarmed. Eats every 2-3 weeks, fasts before a molt.

species.name: Chilean rose tarantula
species.note: Leg span about 15 cm (body length derived at a third of the span). A calm, terrestrial desert-scrub tarantula: dark brown with a rose-pink sheen on the carapace and legs. Moody: sits for weeks, then walks; known for long fasts.

species.name: Curly hair tarantula
species.note: Leg span about 17 cm (body length derived at a third of the span; the care sheet gives 8 cm). A hardy, stocky terrestrial burrower covered in long curled bronze-gold hairs over a black body. Hungry and active; kicks hairs when upset.

species.name: Pinktoe tarantula
species.note: Body about 5 cm (assumed), leg span 12-13 cm. An arboreal tarantula: black-brown with pink-tipped toes, lives in a silk tube against bark or the wall. Fast and jumpy; squirts feces when startled. Needs a tall, ventilated enclosure.

species.name: Emperor scorpion
species.note: Up to 15-20 cm with the tail straight; drawn as 12 cm with the tail arched over the back and the claws forward. Glossy black, the big claws blackish-red, the tail tip amber. Burrows under bark and rock, nocturnal, a mild sting but a strong pinch; glows blue-green under UV.

species.name: Giant African millipede
species.note: Typically 20-30 cm and a thumb thick: a glossy black-brown tube of rings with reddish-orange legs. Burrows and lives under the substrate, comes out at night to eat, curls into a spiral when handled and may ooze a mild irritant. Needs deep damp substrate.

species.name: Madagascar hissing cockroach
species.note: Adults 5-7 cm and wingless: a glossy mahogany-brown oval with tan edges; the male has horned shoulders. Hisses through its spiracles, can climb glass but not smooth plastic, slow, harmless, lives 2-5 years. A colony or a solitary pet.

species.name: Zebra isopod
species.note: Up to 18 mm: a pill bug in bold black and white stripes. Rolls into a ball when threatened, eats leaf litter and rotting wood, and cleans the enclosure floor. Keep a moist and a dry end. A colony, not a pet to hold.

species.name: Powder blue isopod
species.note: About 1 cm: a flat, fast, slate-blue isopod with a pale powdery bloom that does not roll up. Very prolific, breeds in any damp leaf litter, a good cleanup crew. Likes warmth and moisture.

species.name: Orchid mantis
species.note: The female reaches 6-7 cm, the male half that. White to pale pink, the walking legs flattened like petals, motionless on a flowering stem waiting for flies. Needs warmth, humidity and live flying insects; lives only 5-9 months as an adult.

species.name: Indian stick insect
species.note: Females about 8 cm: a thin brown to green twig with long legs held back and forward in line with the body. Climbs bramble, privet and ivy, freezes or sways like a twig, feigns death when handled. Females lay eggs without mating; a colony is all female.

species.name: Purple pincher hermit crab
species.note: About 7.5 cm with its shell (3-6 in is quoted): a tan to orange-red body, a purple left claw, in a borrowed turbo shell. A land crab: climbs, digs to molt for weeks, needs 75-85 F, 70-80 % humidity and both fresh and salt water to dip in. Lives 10+ years.
